coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House
record.summary: The Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House is an 80-bedroom nonprofit facility of about 89,000 sq ft (the Assessor's property area; OCII's 2014 resolution describes a planned 96,000 sq ft facility) at 540 Mission Bay Blvd North (Mission Bay Block 7 East), providing free housing for families of patients primarily receiving treatment at UCSF Mission Bay Medical Center. DataSF Assessor records date its construction to 2016, and Family House's own history page says it opened in Mission Bay in 2016; the month differs by source (see open questions).

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8711227 (2,828 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints (mblr SF8711227)); 99% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 69% of the lot.

changes.text: The map notes said OCII's commission meeting was March 18; OCII's own Resolution No. 10-2014 is dated March 4, 2014, and the notes now say so (and that Citizen Portal is an automated summary, not a primary source). The 2012 parcel recording date now cites the DataSF Parcels record. The record said Family House serves children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital; OCII's resolution says families of patients primarily treated at UCSF Mission Bay Medical Center, so the summary and notes now use that wording. Founding year, the earlier Judah St. building, nightly capacity, families served and 'low-income-qualified' were removed because no readable cited page states them. The summary's ~92,000 sq ft was replaced by the Assessor's 89,197 sq ft with OCII's planned 96,000 sq ft noted, the Nancy & Stephen Grand name now cites Family House's rooms page, and the milestone no longer calls OCII successor to the 'Mission Bay Redevelopment Agency'. The Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural. The May 2016 opening rests on a UCSF page that blocks automated fetches and remains listed among the record's open questions.

open_questions: Month of the 2016 opening: the UCSF News article "New Family House Opens at Mission Bay" (web address dated 2016/05) returned HTTP 403 on 2026-10-12, so its text, and any May 2016 date, has not been read; Potrero View's February 13, 2016 item said the house "opens next month" (that is, March, an expected date written before the event), and a Family House article title seen in a search ("Grand Family House Grand Opening Ribbon Cutting ... March 2, 2016") points to a March ceremony. No source read dates the first families' move-in, so the record shows 2016 only.
The exact month and day of the opening are not settled by any source read; only the year is shown.

A separate Family House article title found in search ('Grand Family House Grand Opening Ribbon Cutting... March 2, 2016') suggests a ribbon-cutting ceremony preceded the May 2016 move-in date, but that page is no longer available (page not found) and its content could not be confirmed -- not used as a citation here.

No readable source says the Family House serves children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital specifically; OCII's 2014 resolution describes 'families of patients primarily receiving treatment at UCSF Mission Bay Medical Center'. The founding year (1981), the earlier Judah St. building, capacity (250 people a night), families served (3,000+ a year) and 'low-income-qualified' were removed from the shape notes because no readable cited page states them; Family House's own history page likely does.

record.notes: 5-story, 80-room nonprofit 'home away from home' for families of patients primarily receiving treatment at UCSF Mission Bay Medical Center (OCII Resolution No. 10-2014) -- free lodging ('always 100% free of charge' per Family House's rooms page), run by Family House, Inc. Opened at this Mission Bay location in 2016 (Assessor year built 2016). Assessor's welfare exemption on the parcel matches its nonprofit operation.
